    Analysing PBMCs with bixverse¶

    Python port of the R vignette Analysing PBMCs with bixverse. Original authors: Grant Neilson, Gregor Lueg and Liesbeth François.

    A standard single cell analysis on the PBMC3k data set with bixverse. If you have not read the design choices and the introductory vignette, do so first; this one assumes you know how the SingleCells class, the on-disk storage and the cells-to-keep logic work.

    In [1]:
    Copied! 
    import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import polars as pl

import bixverse as bv
import bixverse.embed
from bixverse.params import NeighboursParams
    import tempfile from pathlib import Path from typing import Literal import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import numpy as np import polars as pl import bixverse as bv import bixverse.embed from bixverse.params import NeighboursParams

    Loading the data¶

    We download the PBMC3k data and load it through the Cell Ranger style MTX reader. The experiment lives in a directory: the cell- and gene-major binary stores plus a DuckDB with obs and var.

    In [2]:
    Copied! 
    pbmc3k_path = bv.io.download_pbmc3k()

tempdir_pbmc = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()

sc = bv.io.load_mtx(
    Path(tempdir_pbmc.name) / "pbmc3k",
    bv.io.get_cell_ranger_params(pbmc3k_path),
    verbose=True,
)

sc

    Quality control¶

    Gene set proportions¶

    First up, the proportion of counts that map to mitochondrial and ribosomal genes per cell. They land directly in the obs table in the DuckDB.

    In [5]:
    Copied! 
    gs_of_interest = {
    "MT": var.filter(pl.col("gene_symbol").str.contains("^MT-"))["gene_id"].to_list(),
    "Ribo": var.filter(pl.col("gene_symbol").str.contains("^RP[SL]"))[
        "gene_id"
    ].to_list(),
}

bv.qc.gene_set_proportions(sc, gs_of_interest, streaming=False, verbose=True)

sc.obs().head()

    MAD outlier detection¶

    Per-cell QC metrics and MAD-based outlier detection flag the problematic cells. run_cell_qc returns a CellQc that carries the metrics, the per-metric outlier calls and a combined outlier vector.

    In [6]:
    Copied! 
    qc_df = sc.obs(cols=["cell_id", "lib_size", "nnz", "MT"])

metrics = {
    "log10_lib_size": np.log10(qc_df["lib_size"].to_numpy()),
    "log10_nnz": np.log10(qc_df["nnz"].to_numpy()),
    "MT": qc_df["MT"].to_numpy(),
}

directions: dict[str, Literal["twosided", "below", "above"]] = {
    "log10_lib_size": "twosided",
    "log10_nnz": "twosided",
    "MT": "above",
}

qc = bv.qc.run_cell_qc(
    metrics,
    sc.cells_to_keep,
    directions=directions,
    threshold=3.0,
)

print(f"{qc.combined.sum()} of {qc.combined.size} cells flagged")

qc.thresholds
    qc_df = sc.obs(cols=["cell_id", "lib_size", "nnz", "MT"]) metrics = { "log10_lib_size": np.log10(qc_df["lib_size"].to_numpy()), "log10_nnz": np.log10(qc_df["nnz"].to_numpy()), "MT": qc_df["MT"].to_numpy(), } directions: dict[str, Literal["twosided", "below", "above"]] = { "log10_lib_size": "twosided", "log10_nnz": "twosided", "MT": "above", } qc = bv.qc.run_cell_qc( metrics, sc.cells_to_keep, directions=directions, threshold=3.0, ) print(f"{qc.combined.sum()} of {qc.combined.size} cells flagged") qc.thresholds

    Filtering cells¶

    We store the outlier flag in obs and then set the cells to keep. From here on every downstream method (HVG selection, PCA, ...) only sees the retained cells.

    In [9]:
    Copied! 
    sc.add_obs(pl.DataFrame({"cell_idx": qc.cell_idx, "outlier": qc.combined}))

sc.set_cells_to_keep(qc.cell_idx[~qc.combined])

sc
    sc.add_obs(pl.DataFrame({"cell_idx": qc.cell_idx, "outlier": qc.combined})) sc.set_cells_to_keep(qc.cell_idx[~qc.combined]) sc

    Feature selection, PCA and neighbours¶

    With QC done, the standard pipeline: highly variable genes, PCA and the nearest neighbours.

    In [10]:
    Copied! 
    bv.pp.find_hvg(sc, hvg_no=2000, verbose=True)

bv.pp.calculate_pca(sc, no_pcs=30, sparse_svd=True)

# the data is so tiny that an exhaustive kNN search is faster than building an
# approximate nearest neighbour index
bv.graph.find_neighbours(
    sc, neighbours_params=NeighboursParams(knn_method="exhaustive")
)
    bv.pp.find_hvg(sc, hvg_no=2000, verbose=True) bv.pp.calculate_pca(sc, no_pcs=30, sparse_svd=True) # the data is so tiny that an exhaustive kNN search is faster than building an # approximate nearest neighbour index bv.graph.find_neighbours( sc, neighbours_params=NeighboursParams(knn_method="exhaustive") )

    Clustering and marker detection¶

    Leiden clustering¶

    Leiden clustering, then differential expression across all clusters. Louvain is there too if you want it, but Leiden has the better properties, see Traag et al..

    In [11]:
    Copied! 
    bv.graph.find_clusters(sc, res=1.0, name="leiden_clusters")

all_markers = bv.de.find_all_markers(sc, "leiden_clusters").with_columns(
    pl.col("gene_id").replace_strict(ensembl_to_symbol).alias("gene_symbol")
)

all_markers.filter(pl.col("fdr") <= 0.05).sort(
    pl.col("lfc").abs(), descending=True
).head()
    bv.graph.find_clusters(sc, res=1.0, name="leiden_clusters") all_markers = bv.de.find_all_markers(sc, "leiden_clusters").with_columns( pl.col("gene_id").replace_strict(ensembl_to_symbol).alias("gene_symbol") ) all_markers.filter(pl.col("fdr") <= 0.05).sort( pl.col("lfc").abs(), descending=True ).head()

    Fast clustering¶

    For large data sets there is an accelerated clustering: k-means first (floor(4 * sqrt(N)) centroids by default), then Louvain or Leiden on a graph over the centroids, across a set of resolutions. The centroid graph options, the seed stability statistics and how the result compares against the full graph clustering are in the clustering and annotation vignette.

    In [12]:
    Copied! 
    fast_cluster_res = bv.graph.fast_cluster(
    sc,
    resolutions=(2.0, 1.0, 0.5),
    # also return the k-means clustering
    return_kmeans=True,
)

fast_cluster_res.memberships.head()
    fast_cluster_res = bv.graph.fast_cluster( sc, resolutions=(2.0, 1.0, 0.5), # also return the k-means clustering return_kmeans=True, ) fast_cluster_res.memberships.head()

    Dimensionality reduction¶

    UMAP and t-SNE, both from manifolds-rs (the embed extra).

    In [15]:
    Copied! 
    bv.embed.umap(sc)

# perplexity 10 is the default; `bv.embed.tsne_defaults()` has the rest
bv.embed.tsne(sc)
    bv.embed.umap(sc) # perplexity 10 is the default; `bv.embed.tsne_defaults()` has the rest bv.embed.tsne(sc)

    bv.pl (the plots extra) has the basic plots. embedding_plot shows an embedding coloured by an obs column:

    In [16]:
    Copied! 
    bv.pl.embedding_plot(
    sc,
    "umap",
    "leiden_clusters",
    label_by="leiden_clusters",
    discrete=True,
)
plt.show()
    bv.pl.embedding_plot( sc, "umap", "leiden_clusters", label_by="leiden_clusters", discrete=True, ) plt.show()

    We annotate the PBMCs with scType from Ianevski et al. (2022). prepare_cell_markers gets the markers into shape, calc_sc_type_scores scores every cell and score_clusters summarises the scores per cluster into a cell type call.

    In [20]:
    Copied! 
    cell_markers_df = pl.DataFrame(
    {"gene_symbol": list(cell_markers), "cell_type": list(cell_markers.values())}
).join(var.select("gene_symbol", "gene_id"), on="gene_symbol")

marker_list = bv.annotate.prepare_cell_markers(sc, cell_markers_df)

sctype_scores = bv.annotate.calc_sc_type_scores(sc, marker_list)

leiden = sc.obs(cols=["leiden_clusters"], filtered=True)["leiden_clusters"]

cell_type_anno = bv.annotate.score_clusters(sctype_scores, leiden.to_numpy())

cell_type_anno

    Back into obs it goes.

    In [21]:
    Copied! 
    sc.add_obs(
    sc.obs(cols=["cell_idx", "leiden_clusters"], filtered=True)
    .join(
        cell_type_anno.select(
            pl.col("cluster_id").alias("leiden_clusters"),
            pl.col("cell_type").alias("sc_type"),
        ),
        on="leiden_clusters",
        how="left",
    )
    .select("cell_idx", "sc_type")
)

bv.pl.embedding_plot(
    sc,

    label_by="sc_type",
    discrete=True,
)
plt.show()
    sc.add_obs( sc.obs(cols=["cell_idx", "leiden_clusters"], filtered=True) .join( cell_type_anno.select( pl.col("cluster_id").alias("leiden_clusters"), pl.col("cell_type").alias("sc_type"), ), on="leiden_clusters", how="left", ) .select("cell_idx", "sc_type") ) bv.pl.embedding_plot( sc, "umap", "sc_type", label_by="sc_type", discrete=True, ) plt.show()
